Diploma programme · Language studies

Diploma in English

A proposed programme designed to strengthen practical English communication for study, work and everyday situations.

Duration: 1 yearCommunication skillsFour language skillsPractical learning

Programme overview

Students develop their ability to understand and use English in common academic, professional and social contexts. Learning can combine guided lessons, practice activities and applied tasks.

Indicative modules

  • Grammar and vocabulary development
  • Reading and listening comprehension
  • Writing: paragraphs, emails and reports
  • Speaking, pronunciation and presentations
  • English for academic and workplace communication

Learning outcomes

  • Communicate information and ideas more clearly
  • Understand a range of written and spoken texts
  • Prepare organised written work for familiar purposes
  • Participate in conversations and short presentations

Assessment and entry

Suggested assessment: written assignments, speaking tasks, listening and reading activities, presentations and quizzes.

Entry requirements: to be confirmed by the campus; a placement assessment may be used to identify the appropriate learning level.

Programme structure, level, duration, entry requirements, assessment weighting, fees and award status must be approved and confirmed by Avenoora before enrolment or publication as final facts.

Diploma programme · Digital skills

Diploma in Information Communication Technology

A proposed programme introducing essential computing, digital productivity and information technology concepts for modern study and work.

Duration: 1 yearComputer fundamentalsDigital productivityApplied ICT

Programme overview

Students build foundational knowledge of computer systems, software applications, online tools and safe digital practices. Practical activities can help learners apply ICT skills to everyday tasks.

Indicative modules

  • Computer fundamentals and operating systems
  • Word processing and document preparation
  • Spreadsheets and presentation software
  • Internet, email and online collaboration
  • Introduction to databases and information systems
  • Cybersecurity, privacy and digital citizenship

Learning outcomes

  • Use common computer devices and applications
  • Create and format documents, spreadsheets and presentations
  • Find, evaluate and communicate information online
  • Apply basic cybersecurity and data-protection practices
  • Complete a practical digital task or project

Assessment and entry

Suggested assessment: practical computer assignments, document and spreadsheet tasks, quizzes, presentations and an applied project.

Entry requirements: to be confirmed by the campus. Basic computer familiarity may be helpful but should not be advertised as compulsory unless formally adopted.

Software, equipment, practical facilities, programme duration, fees, entry criteria and award status must be confirmed by the campus. Do not imply vendor certification or external accreditation unless formally obtained.

Diploma programme · People and organisations

Diploma in Human Resource Management

A proposed programme covering the fundamentals of managing people, supporting employees and contributing to effective workplace practices.

Duration: 1 yearPeople managementWorkplace practicesProfessional skills

Programme overview

Students explore the role of human resource management in organisations, from workforce planning and recruitment to employee development, performance and workplace relations.

Indicative modules

  • Introduction to Human Resource Management
  • Workforce planning and job analysis
  • Recruitment and selection
  • Training and employee development
  • Performance management
  • Employee engagement and workplace communication
  • Introduction to employment law and ethical practice

Learning outcomes

  • Explain core HR functions and their organisational purpose
  • Describe fair recruitment and selection practices
  • Identify approaches to training and performance support
  • Communicate professionally about workplace matters
  • Recognise the importance of confidentiality, fairness and compliance

Assessment and entry

Suggested assessment: case-study assignments, recruitment exercises, HR document preparation, presentations, group tasks and quizzes.

Entry requirements: to be confirmed by the campus and published in the official admissions policy.

Employment-law content must be kept current and relevant to the jurisdiction taught. Duration, entry requirements, fees, assessment rules and award status require institutional confirmation.

Diploma programme · Business studies

Diploma in Business Management

A proposed programme introducing key management concepts and the practical skills used to support business operations and decision-making.

Duration: 1 yearManagement principlesBusiness operationsDecision-making

Programme overview

Students gain an introductory understanding of how organisations plan, organise and manage resources. Activities can connect management theory with everyday business situations.

Indicative modules

  • Introduction to Business and Management
  • Principles of Management and Leadership
  • Marketing fundamentals
  • Business communication
  • Introduction to accounting and finance
  • Operations and project management
  • Entrepreneurship and business planning

Learning outcomes

  • Describe core business functions and management roles
  • Apply basic planning and organisational techniques
  • Interpret simple business information for decisions
  • Communicate and collaborate in a team
  • Prepare a basic business plan or project proposal

Assessment and entry

Suggested assessment: individual assignments, business case studies, group projects, presentations, quizzes and a business-plan task.

Entry requirements: to be confirmed by the campus and stated in the published admissions policy.

The module list is indicative, not an approved syllabus. Confirm the programme level, learning hours, duration, entry requirements, fees and award status before advertising enrolment.

Diploma programme · Food hygiene and safety

Diploma in Food Safety

A proposed programme introducing safe food handling, hygiene controls and practical ways to reduce food-safety risks.

Duration: 1 yearFood hygieneHazard awarenessSafe handling

Programme overview

Students learn why food can become unsafe and how good hygiene, appropriate storage, cleaning and handling practices help protect consumers throughout food preparation and service.

Indicative modules

  • Introduction to food safety and foodborne illness
  • Personal hygiene and safe food handling
  • Food contamination and cross-contamination prevention
  • Time and temperature control
  • Cleaning, sanitation and pest awareness
  • Food storage, receiving and traceability
  • Introduction to HACCP principles and food-safety records

Learning outcomes

  • Identify common biological, chemical and physical hazards
  • Explain how contamination and foodborne illness can occur
  • Apply appropriate hygiene and safe-handling practices
  • Describe basic temperature-control and cleaning procedures
  • Recognise the purpose of food-safety management systems

Assessment and entry

Suggested assessment: practical demonstrations, hygiene inspection exercises, hazard-identification assignments, case studies and quizzes.

Entry requirements: to be confirmed by the campus. Any practical or workplace requirements must be stated clearly before admission.

Food-safety teaching should be aligned with applicable local regulations and current authoritative guidance. This programme description does not itself confer a statutory food-handler licence or external certification.
